Machine-readable sources

Short excerpts from the committed synthetic sources. No real legislation is encoded.

Axiom RuleSpec — machine-readable excerpt

Inputs and derived judgments are declared in structured YAML. The full source compiles to an Axiom artifact; this static page does not execute it.

- name: procurement_obligation
    kind: derived
    entity: Procurement
    dtype: Judgment
    sources:
      - citation: "Synthetic procurement policy s.1 (fictional)"
        url: https://example.org/synthetic-procurement-policy
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-01-01'
        formula: facts_complete and covered_body and contract_scope_met and not exception_applies
  - name: open_source_consideration_required
    kind: derived
    entity: Procurement

Axiom RuleSpec source

Legalese L4 — machine-readable excerpt

CONSIDER/WHEN steps, MAYBE values and a deontic MUST duty are expressed directly. The full synthetic page shows the readable ladder and dependency graph.

`procurement outcome` covered_body contract_scope_met exception_applies contract_value MEANS
    CONSIDER covered_body
    WHEN NOTHING THEN Indeterminate
    WHEN JUST FALSE THEN NotApplicable
    WHEN JUST TRUE THEN
        CONSIDER contract_scope_met
        WHEN NOTHING THEN Indeterminate
        WHEN JUST FALSE THEN OutsideScope
        WHEN JUST TRUE THEN
            CONSIDER exception_applies
            WHEN NOTHING THEN Indeterminate
            WHEN JUST TRUE THEN ExceptionApplies
            WHEN JUST FALSE THEN
                IF contract_value >= 100000
                THEN OpenSourceConsiderationRequired
                ELSE RequirementWithoutOpenSource

DECLARE Party IS ONE OF ContractingAuthority

Evaluation order

  1. Are the required facts complete?

    If true
    Continue to coverage
    If false
    Indeterminate

    Citation: Synthetic procurement policy s.3 (fictional) SP-3. Missing facts are not treated as false.

  2. Is the public body covered?

    If true
    Continue to scope
    If false
    Not applicable

    Citation: Synthetic procurement policy s.1 (fictional) SP-1. Coverage is a condition, not a legal conclusion.

  3. Is the contract within scope?

    If true
    Continue to exceptions
    If false
    Outside scope

    Citation: Synthetic procurement policy s.1 (fictional) SP-1. Scope is checked before the exception.

  4. Does an exception apply?

    If true
    Exception applies
    If false
    Continue to the threshold

    Citation: Synthetic procurement policy s.1 (fictional) SP-1. An exception removes the requirement; it does not create a new one.

  5. Is the contract value at least USD 100,000?

    If true
    Open-source consideration required
    If false
    Requirement without open-source threshold

    Citation: Synthetic procurement policy s.2 (fictional) SP-2. The boundary value itself meets the threshold.

Accessible text equivalent

Linear explanation

  1. Start with facts_complete. If it is false, stop at Indeterminate (SP-3).
  2. If the facts are complete, check covered_body. If it is false, the outcome is Not applicable (SP-1).
  3. If the body is covered, check contract_scope_met. If it is false, the outcome is Outside scope (SP-1).
  4. If the contract is in scope, check exception_applies. If it is true, the outcome is Exception applies (SP-1).
  5. If no exception applies, compare contract_value with USD 100,000. At or above the threshold, open-source consideration is required (SP-2); below it, the procurement requirement applies without the open-source threshold (SP-2).

Unknown and missing facts

Missing required facts are not treated as false. This synthetic model reports Indeterminate; the renderer does not infer a legal outcome.

Unsupported or out of scope

  • Deontic modality: Obligation, permission and prohibition are not first-class in RuleSpec. L4 can express them with PARTY, MUST, MAY and SHANT.
  • Amendment and version history: Effective dates can be encoded, but a reviewed instrument-version and amendment graph is external metadata; this prototype does not model it.
  • Translation provenance: Neither engine records official, reviewed or machine-assisted translation status. The interface translations here are provisional.
  • Real legal text and citation verification: All sources are fictional. No real instrument, provision, date or legal effect is encoded.
  • Contradiction detection: Both engines applied the ladder order to contradictory facts; neither reported a contradiction.

Known semantic differences

Axiom treats a missing required input as an execution error; the L4 version models missing facts as Indeterminate. Axiom RuleSpec has no deontic modality; its judgment outputs are not duties. The synthetic example does not claim equivalence beyond the tested cases.
